evidence: deck-flicopy: rect-readback /O2 52 differing bytes vs baseline 54 (extent 310 agrees); instruction diff shows only mov ecx/push ecx vs mov eax/push eax swaps for the stride and width loads; /Oy- stays 320 extent-blocked; applied to decode_fli_copy.

deck-dbrb: rect-readback on decode_byte_run /O2 diverges from byte 6 (push edi appears, xor ebx,ebx zero-store prologue lost), 462 diff bytes vs baseline 287; /Oy- 512 extent-blocked either way; rejected, current spelling kept.
payload.hypothesis: The rect read-back spelling (`rect[2] = rect[0] + width`) is context-dependent rather than family-wide: it is 2 bytes closer in decode_fli_copy /O2 (54->52 diff, remaining deltas are ecx-vs-eax choices for immediately-pushed values) but 175 bytes worse in decode_byte_run (287->462) because it destroys the early xor-zero-store prologue, so a winning rect spelling must be scored per function before editing.
